statement.excerpt: That same month, Cursor’s AWS costs — which I believe are the minority of its cloud compute costs — exploded by 104% (or by $6.48 million), and never returned to their previous levels.
statement.document_title: This Is How Much Anthropic and Cursor Spend On Amazon Web Services

from_speaker: which I believe are the minority of its cloud compute costs
never returned to their previous levels
our_interpretation: That same month means June 2025, compared with May 2025.
Never returned is bounded by the post's records through September 2025; it is not an indefinite forecast.
Previous levels means the May monthly AWS bill. Each July–September bill must remain above that baseline.
The 104% figure is treated as an approximate description of roughly doubling, not a claim of precision finer than the displayed rounded dollar figures.
The parenthetical minority assertion is a separate, hedged component requiring total cloud-compute costs.
The accounting basis is estimate because these are externally reported private-company bills, not identified company financial statements.
criteria.support_condition: Independent May and June invoices establish an increase of approximately 104% and $6.48 million, and each July–September invoice exceeds May's level. The minority component additionally requires AWS to account for less than half of comparable total cloud-compute costs.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Independent invoices show a materially different June increase, or at least one July–September bill returns to May's level or below. Comparable total-cost records showing AWS at least half of cloud-compute spending would contradict the parenthetical component only.
